title: Talking with AI: an interlocutor, not a curator

outline.heading: Start with the most inconvenient fact

points.text: The evidence says that what works in digital programmes is a human in the loop.
The largest online randomised trial in this area — Segal and colleagues (JAMA Psychiatry, 2020; 460 participants) — showed an advantage of an online programme over usual care.
The detail usually lost in retellings: the programme ran with coach support, not as a purely self-guided app.
Hence the course's honest position: AI sits here between sessions, not instead of people.
The boundaries aren't invented by the course — they're assembled from normative documents and from the few places where an effect has actually been shown

outline.heading: What the companion may not do — and why

points.text: The American Psychological Association Health Advisory on generative AI chatbots and wellness applications (November 2025) is the weightiest normative source available today.
That is a vendor statement rather than research — an admission against interest — and it bears directly on our construction: an eight-week course with a companion is precisely a long interaction.
